result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane roadway passing under a heavy rail bridge with significant sightline obstructions. While a marked crosswalk is present, the markings are faded and the overall design prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Blind Spots from Bridge Piers
hazards.description: The large stone bridge supports create significant visual obstructions between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left, where the road passes under the bridge arches

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Long Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge or dedicated pedestrian signalization.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Refresh the crossing with thermoplastic high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight past the bridge piers.

result.summary: The environment features a wide multi-lane arterial with integrated rail tracks and a marked zebra crosswalk. Pedestrians face a long, unprotected crossing distance across multiple lanes of traffic without a central refuge island.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The roadway is very wide, requiring pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic and rail tracks in a single stage without a refuge.

hazards.name: Rail Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway can be a trip hazard for pedestrians or a slip hazard in wet conditions.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island between the travel lanes and the rail tracks to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking or shoulder lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The intersection features a wide multi-lane roadway with significant crossing distances and no pedestrian refuge islands. While sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the lack of high-visibility crosswalk markings and the scale of the road create a challenging environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The crosswalk markings across the main thoroughfare are faded or incomplete, reducing visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental or ladder style markings to improve visibility of the crossing area for approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a complex intersection with trolley tracks and a large bridge overpass that creates significant visual obstructions. While marked crosswalks and sidewalks are present, the long crossing distances and lack of pedestrian-scale safety features like refuge islands make it a challenging environment for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Exposed metal rails in the pavement create a trip hazard and can be slippery when wet.

hazards.name: Bridge Abutments
hazards.description: Large concrete structures block sightlines between pedestrians and turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the wide roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Improved Lighting
interventions.description: Enhance lighting levels under the bridge and at the intersection to improve pedestrian visibility.
